WHY: after editing a booking's location, the calendar references are written with undefined externalCalendarId and credentialId. WHY: the patch fails for Meet bookings without a matching destination calendar, so the description never gets the hangout link. A destination calendar with no credentialId is also ignored. S4.label: bug
S4.suggestionContent: WHAT: the fallback `find(cal => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` is evaluated only when externalCalendarId is falsy, so it can never match any calendar. WHY: updateEvent and deleteEvent no longer fall back to the destination calendar's externalId and pass an undefined calendarId to Google. S5.label: bug
S5.suggestionContent: WHAT: team members' destination calendars are appended with `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...)`, which does nothing when evt.destinationCalendar is null. WHY: for a COLLECTIVE event where neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar, the other hosts' calendars are silently dropped. HOW: assign a new array, e.g. `evt.destinationCalendar = [...(evt.destinationCalendar ?? []), ...teamDestinationCalendars]`.

S6.label: bug
S6.suggestionContent: WHAT: createEvent always uses the first destination calendar's externalId and ignores which credential is creating the event. EventManager now calls createEvent once per host credential with the same multi-host event. WHY: for a collective event, the second host's Office365 credential posts to the first host's calendar id, so the call fails or lands in the wrong calendar. The Lark service has the same pattern. HOW: accept the credentialId argument and pick `destinationCalendar.find(c => c.credentialId === credentialId)`, as the Google service does.

S7.suggestionContent: When `evt.destinationCalendar` is null or empty, the destructured `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is undefined. Line 119 then reads `.integration` on it without optional chaining, which throws a TypeError. This happens for Google Meet bookings by a user with no destination calendar, and it aborts event creation instead of falling back to Cal Video. Use optional chaining on the property access.

S8.label: bug
S8.suggestionContent: Destructuring the first element of an empty destinationCalendar array yields undefined, and `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` is then dereferenced without optional chaining. This throws a TypeError for Google Meet bookings with no destination calendar, where it should fall back to Cal Video. Use `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`.

S10.label: bug

S10.label: bug

S1.label: bug
S1.suggestionContent: WHAT: `prisma.credential.update` is called in `getClient`, but `prisma` is never imported in this file. WHY: this fails type-checking and throws a ReferenceError whenever a Salesforce client is constructed, so the Salesforce integration breaks. HOW: add `import prisma from "@calcom/prisma";`.

S2.label: performance
S2.suggestionContent: WHAT: `getClient` now always POSTs to Salesforce's token endpoint and writes the credential to the DB on every service construction. This is done without an expiry check and without going through `refreshOAuthTokens`, so credential sync is bypassed for Salesforce. WHY: every booking or availability call triggers an extra network round trip and DB write, and the sync endpoint is never used for this app. It also throws on any non-'OK' statusText. HOW: only refresh when the token is expired, and call it through `refreshOAuthTokens`.

S3.label: bug
S3.suggestionContent: WHAT: the computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` evaluate to a fixed string like "[object Object]", not a wildcard. The schema therefore requires a numeric property with that literal name. WHY: every parse in sync mode fails and throws 'Invalid refreshed tokens were returned', so credential sync cannot work. HOW: use `z.object({ access_token: z.string() }).passthrough()` and check expiry fields explicitly.

S4.label: bug
S4.suggestionContent: WHAT: when the response lacks `refresh_token`, a literal placeholder "refresh_token" is injected into the parsed data. WHY: callers such as Zoom (`key.refresh_token = newTokens.refresh_token`) and Salesforce persist this data, overwriting the real refresh token with a fake one, which breaks later refreshes. HOW: do not inject a placeholder; leave the field undefined or preserve the existing token in the caller.

S5.label: bug
S5.suggestionContent: WHAT: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the zod safeParse result (`{success, data}`), and that whole object is saved as the credential `key`. WHY: the stored Google credential becomes `{success:true,data:{...}}` and loses its token fields, so the next `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` throws. HOW: store `parseRefreshTokenResponse(...).data`.

S6.label: bug
S6.suggestionContent: WHAT: in sync mode the function returns the raw fetch `Response`, while callers expect the refresh function's shape. Those shapes are axios `{data}` (Zoho, Bigin), the googleapis `res.data`, and the Hubspot token object. WHY: callers read `tokenInfo.data.error`, `res.data`, or `hubspotRefreshToken.expiresIn` on a Response, which yields undefined or a TypeError, so the sync path fails for these apps. HOW: parse the sync response (`await response.json()`) and adapt it to the shape each caller expects, e.g. wrap it as `{ data }`.

S7.label: bug
S7.suggestionContent: WHAT: `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a fetch Response in sync mode, but the code reads `tokenInfo.data.error` as an axios response. WHY: `tokenInfo.data` is undefined on a Response, so this throws a TypeError whenever credential sync is enabled. HOW: normalize the sync response to `{ data: json }` inside `refreshOAuthTokens`, or here before use.

S8.label: bug
S8.suggestionContent: WHAT: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` throws on invalid data, and the previous error logging branch was removed. The line below still relies on `tokenResponse.success`, which is now always true if reached. WHY: a malformed Microsoft token response previously just logged and kept the old credentials, but now aborts the whole refresh with a generic error and no logging of the MS response. HOW: keep the safeParse and error logging in the non-sync path, or catch and log the zod error.

S9.label: security
S9.suggestionContent: WHAT: the webhook secret is compared with `!==`, which is not constant-time. WHY: this is the only authentication on an endpoint that overwrites any user's third-party credentials, and the comparison leaks timing information about the secret. HOW: compare with `crypto.timingSafeEqual` over equal-length buffers.

S10.label: bug
S10.suggestionContent: refreshOAuthTokens' third parameter is `userId` and is sent as `calcomUserId` to the sync endpoint, but this call passes `credentialId`. A credential id gets treated as a Cal.com user id, so the wrong user's credentials can be requested or synced. The refreshAccessToken method has no user id available, so pass the credential's userId (add it as a parameter) instead.

S11.label: bug
S11.suggestionContent: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a zod SafeParse result ({success, data}), but the old googleCredentialSchema.parse returned the parsed key. The result is now stored as the credential `key`, so the credential becomes {success:true,data:{...}} and loses the top-level access_token, refresh_token and expiry_date. Later Google auth reads of the credential then fail. Store `.data` of the parsed result instead.

S12.label: security
S12.suggestionContent: `refreshOAuthTokens` expects a Cal.com userId, but this call passes `credentialId`. With credential sync enabled, the sync endpoint receives the credential row id as `calcomUserId`. It can return a different user's OAuth access token, and that token is then stored on this credential and returned to the caller. Pass the owning user's id instead.

S13.label: security
S13.suggestionContent: The webhook secret is compared with `!==`, which leaks timing information. This secret is the only authentication on an endpoint that overwrites any user's app credentials. Compare the hashed or equal-length buffers with crypto.timingSafeEqual instead.

S14.label: security
S14.suggestionContent: The decryption key falls back to an empty string when CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY is unset. A critical key should not have a weak default. Fail fast with an explicit error if the key is missing.

S15.label: bug
S15.suggestionContent: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a zod safeParse result ({success, data}), not the parsed value. The result is saved as the credential `key`, so the DB gets {success:true,data:{...}} instead of the Google credentials. Later reads of access_token and refresh_token then fail. Store `.data` from the parse result.

S16.label: bug
S16.suggestionContent: refreshOAuthTokens takes a userId as its third argument, but the Zoho Bigin code passes `credentialId`. With credential sharing enabled, the sync endpoint is asked for the wrong calcomUserId, so another user's tokens may be fetched or none found. Pass the credential's userId.

S17.label: bug
S17.suggestionContent: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a zod safeParse result ({success, data}), not the parsed credential. Here the whole wrapper is stored as `key`, so the Google credential in the DB becomes {success:true,data:{...}} and later reads of access_token/refresh_token fail. Use the `.data` of the parsed result as the key.

S18.label: bug
S18.suggestionContent: refreshOAuthTokens declares its third parameter as the Cal.com userId (sent as calcomUserId to the sync endpoint), but this caller passes credentialId. With credential sync enabled the endpoint receives a credential id as the user id, so it syncs the wrong user's tokens or none. Pass the credential's userId instead.

S19.label: bug
S19.suggestionContent: In sync mode refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response, but callers such as Google, Zoho CRM and Zoho Bigin read `.data` as with axios or gaxios. `.data` is undefined on a fetch Response, so token.access_token or tokenInfo.data.error throws a TypeError whenever credential sync is enabled. S20.label: bug
S20.suggestionContent: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a zod SafeParse result ({success, data}), but it is assigned to `key` and written to credential.key. The stored Google credential becomes {success:true,data:{...}}, so the next googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key) throws and the credential is permanently broken. S21.label: bug
S21.suggestionContent: refreshOAuthTokens is given `credentialId` as its userId argument. When credential sync is enabled, the sync endpoint is asked for the credential id as `calcomUserId`, which can return another user's tokens or none. The sync path also returns a fetch Response, so `tokenInfo.data` is undefined and the next line throws a TypeError. Pass the credential's userId instead.

S22.label: bug
S22.suggestionContent: The minimum token schema uses computed keys such as `[z.string().toString()]`, which evaluate to a fixed literal string like "ZodString". The schema therefore requires a property with that literal name to be a number, and no real token response has it. With credential sync enabled, every parse fails and throws "Invalid refreshed tokens were returned". Use `.passthrough()` and `z.object({access_token: z.string()})` instead.

S23.label: bug
S23.suggestionContent: When the parsed response has no refresh_token, the code writes the literal placeholder "refresh_token" into it. Callers that merge this data into the stored credential, such as the Office365 calendar and Salesforce services, then overwrite the real refresh token. Later refreshes fail. Only set the placeholder in sync mode, and never overwrite an existing stored token.

S1.label: bug
S1.suggestionContent: WHAT: 2FA is already enabled when the backup-codes step is shown, but only the 'Close' button calls onEnable()/resetState(). Dismissing the dialog with Escape or an outside click only toggles the parent's open flag via onOpenChange. WHY: the parent never invalidates viewer.me, so the switch and badge show 2FA as disabled until a refresh. The modal also stays on the DisplayBackupCodes step, and reopening it shows the old codes screen. S2.label: security
S2.suggestionContent: WHAT: The password check is skipped whenever `credentials.totpCode` is truthy, and the new backup-code branch never validates totpCode. WHY: an attacker with a valid backup code can send a junk totpCode plus the backupCode and log in without the password. This turns a second-factor credential into a sole credential. HOW: skip the password check only for the legitimate TOTP-only flow, for example when `credentials.totpCode && !credentials.backupCode`. Better, always verify the password for CAL-provider users unless that flow is explicitly authorised.

S3.label: bug
S3.suggestionContent: `expect(locator.isChecked()).toBeTruthy()` asserts on an un-awaited Promise, so it always passes. The enable flow now ends on the backup-codes dialog, which this test never closes, so the test cannot detect a failure to enable 2FA. Close the dialog via `backup-codes-close` and assert `[data-testid=two-factor-switch][data-state="checked"]` is visible, as the second test does.

S4.label: bug
S4.suggestionContent: The backup-code download and copy checks only assert the filename and a toast, so they would pass if the file or clipboard held wrong or empty content. Read the downloaded file (`download.path()`) and compare it with the backup codes stored for the user, and check the clipboard text.

S5.label: bug
S5.suggestionContent: The backup code is verified against a blob read earlier and then written back as a whole re-encrypted blob, with no lock or compare-and-set. Two concurrent logins with the same code both pass verification, so a single-use code is accepted twice. Concurrent logins with different codes overwrite each other's update and restore a consumed code. Make the consume step atomic, for example a transaction or conditional update (updateMany where backupCodes equals the value originally read, and fail the login if count is 0).

S6.label: security
S6.suggestionContent: resetState() does not clear the plaintext backupCodes state or revoke the blob URL in backupCodesUrl. After the dialog is closed or cancelled, the sensitive backup codes stay in memory and the blob URL still serves them. Clear both and call URL.revokeObjectURL when the dialog is closed.

S7.label: bug
S7.suggestionContent: The log message says "cannot proceed with backup code login", but this handler disables 2FA and has no login step. It was copied from the login flow and will mislead anyone reading server logs. Change it to describe disabling 2FA with a backup code.

S8.label: bug
S8.suggestionContent: The component in BackupCode.tsx is named `TwoFactor`, which is the same name as the TOTP component in TwoFactor.tsx. The name suggests the wrong component and makes stack traces and React devtools ambiguous. Rename it to `BackupCode`.

S9.label: security
S9.suggestionContent: The password check at line 121 is skipped whenever `credentials.totpCode` is non-empty, but the new backup-code branch never validates `totpCode`. A request with a junk `totpCode` plus a valid `backupCode` therefore authenticates without the password being verified. Skip the password check only when no backup code is supplied (e.g. `!credentials.totpCode && !credentials.backupCode`), or verify the password inside the backup-code branch.

S10.label: security
S10.suggestionContent: The user-supplied backup code is compared to the stored codes using `Array.indexOf`, which is a short-circuiting, non-constant-time string comparison and leaks timing information. Compare each code with `crypto.timingSafeEqual` over equal-length buffers, without early exit.

S1.label: bug
S1.suggestionContent: getAuthorizationConditions() always returns a non-null Prisma.Sql, so the `else if (filterConditions)` and final `else` (NOTHING_CONDITION) branches in getBaseConditions can never run. The code suggests a filter-only or nothing fallback that cannot happen. Simplify it to: if filterConditions, combine with auth; otherwise return auth.

S1.label: security
S1.suggestionContent: WHAT: Post#cook returns `raw` verbatim for raw_html posts, and the raw comes from remote RSS or scraped HTML that was never sanitized. WHY: script or event-handler HTML in a feed item or page is stored and rendered unescaped (`raw post.cooked` in embed/best.html.erb and in normal topic views), so it executes in the forum's origin. HOW: sanitize the HTML before storing or returning it, for example with the Sanitize gem and a tag/attribute whitelist, in TopicEmbed.import or in this branch of cook.

S2.label: bug
S2.suggestionContent: WHAT: `i.content.scrub` is called without a nil check, and one failing item aborts the loop. WHY: RSS items that only provide a description leave `content` nil, so NoMethodError stops the whole poll and no later items are imported. HOW: fall back to the description and skip items with no content, for example `raw = i.content || i.description; next if raw.blank?`.

S3.label: performance
S3.suggestionContent: WHAT: perform_retrieve runs a full synchronous feed fetch and import (`Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})`) for every uncached embed URL. WHY: the throttle is per URL, so many distinct embed URLs trigger repeated full feed downloads and imports of every item. The `open(feed_url)` call has no timeout, so a slow feed ties up Sidekiq workers. HOW: throttle feed polling globally with a redis key, and add a timeout to the feed fetch.

S4.label: bug
S4.suggestionContent: WHAT: The template closes the conditional with `<%- end if %>`, which is a trailing `if` modifier on `end`. WHY: it is a syntax hazard, because the following template output becomes the modifier's condition. The header branches may then render incorrectly or the template may raise a SyntaxError. HOW: use `<%- end %>`.

S5.label: bug
S5.suggestionContent: Protocol-relative URLs (`//host/path`) start with '/', so they are treated as site-relative. The leading-slash strip then rewrites `//cdn.other.com/a.png` to `http://eviltrout.com/cdn.other.com/a.png`, which points at the wrong host. Skip values that start with `//`, or resolve them against the scheme, for both `a[href]` and `img[src]`.

S6.label: bug
